help.recurring.content.en: Recurring messages repeat automatically - daily, on chosen weekdays, or monthly. How to create: 1. Tap Recurring Message. 2. Pick the channel and the interval (daily/weekly/monthly). 3. Set the send time. 4. Send the content and confirm. Free plan: {recurring_free} recurring message. Premium: unlimited. Manage them from Message List - edit time, pause, resume, or delete. Recurring messages expire after {recurring_expiry_days} days. See also: Pause & Resume for temporary stopping.

help.delete.content.en: Remove scheduled or recurring messages you no longer need. How to delete: • From Message List: tap the 🗑 trash icon next to a message → confirm. • Use 🗑 Delete All at the bottom of the list — it removes all scheduled and recurring messages at once after a confirmation that shows exactly how many messages will go. • Use 🗑 Delete by ID and enter a job ID to remove one specific message (scheduled IDs look like s482913_7, recurring IDs like r482913_7 — you can copy them from the list). What happens after deletion: • Deleted scheduled messages are removed from the queue and will NOT be sent. • Deleted recurring messages are stopped and removed from the scheduler. • Deletion is permanent — it cannot be undone. Tip: to find a job ID first, use Message List or /search. Removing a channel is different — see Remove a Channel.

help.feedback.content.en: Every ticket goes to a human. Open Feedback in the bot (or /feedback), pick a category, and describe the issue — attach a file or screenshot if it helps. What happens next • You get a ticket number immediately. • Replies arrive in the bot chat; you can continue the conversation in the same thread. • My requests shows the status of every ticket you filed. Bug reports with concrete details (job ID, time, what you expected vs. what happened) get fixed fastest. Keep it clean Feedback must not contain offensive language. One mild expression triggers a warning (the message is still sent); heavily offensive messages are blocked, and 3 warnings temporarily block new feedback. Mistaken flags can be reported from the warning itself.

help.search.content.en: The search tool finds any scheduled or recurring message by its text — no scrolling through the calendar needed. How to search 1. Tap Search on the main menu (second page) or send /search. 2. Type a keyword or phrase. 3. The bot lists every matching scheduled and recurring message with its job ID and send time. 4. Results show job ID and send time — open one and you get the same preview and edit/delete controls as the Message List. What is searched • The text content of all scheduled messages. • The text content of all recurring messages. • Job IDs such as s_123 or r_456. Search is case-insensitive, matches partial words ("hel" finds "hello"), and covers all your messages across every channel at once. Narrowing results Use more specific words — the bot matches any of them. To browse by channel or date instead of keyword, the Message List and Calendar tools are the better fit.

help.calendar.content.en: See all your scheduled messages on a monthly calendar. How to Access: 1. Click Calendar on the main menu (page 2) or use /calendar 2. Select a channel (if you have multiple) 3. Browse the month — each day shows scheduled send times Features: • Navigate between months with Previous / Next buttons • Both scheduled (one-time) and recurring messages appear • Recurring messages are expanded across the month based on their schedule • Times are shown in your channel’s timezone Tips: • Use the calendar to spot conflicts or gaps in your schedule • If you don’t see a message, check its timezone setting • For channel-specific views, pick a channel when prompted See also: Timezone Settings and Message List.

help.formatting.content.en: You can use Telegram markdown-style formatting in your messages: **bold** — bold __italic__ — italic ___underline___ — underline ~~strikethrough~~ — strikethrough ||spoiler|| — spoiler `code` — inline code ```block``` — code block [text](url) — text link Note: URLs in text are not automatically clickable in sent messages. Use inline buttons for clickable links. ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Inline Buttons — Full Guide ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Add clickable buttons below any post. There is no button-builder in the bot — just type the markup into your message text (usually at the end). Basic Syntax <inline>Button Text<link="https://url.com"> Multiple Buttons (Each on its own row) <inline>Buy Now<link="https://shop.com"> <inline>Learn More<link="https://info.com"> Side by Side with -- <inline>Buy<link="https://shop.com"> -- <inline>Info<link="https://info.com"> Result: [Buy] [Info] (same row) New Row with // <inline>Catalog<link="https://shop.com"> // <inline>Support<link="https://support.com"> Result: [Catalog] [Support] Full Layout Example <inline>Catalog<link="https://shop.com"> -- <inline>Sale<link="https://shop.com/sale"> // <inline>Reviews<link="https://shop.com/reviews"> -- <inline>Support<link="https://support.com"> Result: [Catalog] [Sale] [Reviews] [Support] Button Colors Add style="success" (green), style="primary" (blue) or style="danger" (red) inside the tag: <inline>Buy Now<link="https://shop.com" style="success"> -- <inline>Remove<link="https://shop.com/remove" style="danger"> Unknown styles are ignored. Important: • Use full URLs with https:// • Keep button text short (a few words) so it fits on phone screens • The markup lines are removed from the published post — buttons appear BELOW the message text Examples • Link button: <inline>Visit Site<link="https://example.com"> • Side by side: <inline>Like<link="https://t.me/yourbot?start=like"> -- <inline>Dislike<link="https://t.me/yourbot?start=dislike"> Callback Buttons <inline>Action Name<callback="action_data"> Callback buttons send data back to the bot instead of opening a link — use them for actions, confirmations, and interactive posts. They follow the same layout rules (-- for the same row, // for a new row) and can be mixed with link buttons. Colors work here too: <inline>Confirm<callback="confirm" style="success">. Important: • Callback data is limited to 64 bytes • Malformed <inline> markup shows a warning — fix the syntax and resend • Callback buttons only work when the bot recognizes the data — you'll be warned before scheduling if a callback has no matching handler

help.admins_limits.content.en: All message-related limits are counted per channel, never per user. Who counts: every admin of the channel — the Main Owner and everyone else — contributes to and shares one single quota. Two admins scheduling for the same channel consume the same budget. Monthly send limit (Free): counts messages actually sent to the channel during the current calendar month — up to {monthly_sent_free}. The counter never drops when messages are deleted; it resets on the 1st of the next month, or immediately when Premium becomes active for the channel. Pending queue cap: up to {scheduled_free} scheduled messages can wait to be sent at once (per channel, shared). Pending scheduled cap: messages waiting to be sent for the channel, shared across all admins. Recurring limit: active recurring messages for the channel, again shared. Premium is per channel: if any admin activates Premium, the channel gets the Premium limits for everyone who uses it, while your other channels stay unaffected. This prevents the classic free-plan loophole where several admins each connect the same channel to multiply the free limits — the quota is on the channel itself.

help.admins_permissions.content.en: The Main Owner manages an RBAC-style permission list for every admin of the channel. What can be controlled: • Scheduling messages • Creating recurring messages • Viewing statistics • Leaderboard access • Exporting data • Managing messages (edit/delete) • Managing sender bots Editing: the owner opens an admin's profile and toggles permissions. Changes are collected into a draft — press Save Changes to apply them, and the bot shows a clear summary of exactly what changed before notifying the affected admin. Leaving the editor with unsaved changes prompts you to save or discard. Immediate effect: as soon as permissions are saved, buttons for disabled features disappear from that admin's menu, and enabled ones appear. If the admin taps an old button anyway, the bot replies "You do not have permission…" with a Request permission from the admin button. Auto-revocation: if an admin is removed from the channel in Telegram, or loses the Post Messages permission, all their bot-side permissions are revoked automatically on the next check — no manual cleanup needed. Requests: an admin who lacks a permission can request it (optionally with an explanation). The owner receives a Yes/No request and can send back a reply when declining. Anti-spam: one request per permission per user per week. The owner can also switch off request notifications for a specific admin.

help.admins_transfer.content.en: Transferring the Main Owner role is deliberately protected by multiple confirmation layers. The flow: 1. The current Main Owner opens the target admin's profile and presses Make Main Owner. 2. The bot asks the owner to type a confirmation phrase exactly (GitHub-style), e.g. "I confirm that I transfer management of [channel] to [username]". 3. After the phrase is accepted, a final confirmation button appears — the transfer is not created until it's pressed. 4. A pending transfer request is sent to the target admin, who must accept or decline it. While pending: the current owner can cancel the request at any time, and it expires automatically after 24 hours. On accept: the ownership swap is performed atomically — the target becomes the new Main Owner, the old owner stays as a regular admin with full permissions, and both parties are notified. At every critical step the bot re-validates that the target is still a real admin with Post Messages permission.

help.bot_stats.content.en: Per-channel statistics show how each channel's posts perform: totals, averages for views, comments and reactions, plus top reactions. How: open Statistics (main menu page 2 or /stats) → pick the channel under the overview. The full stats view is delivered via your main bot; each channel row can also deep-link straight into the sender bot that posts there. Comment attribution (top commentators) works once the bot is in your channel's linked discussion group. These stats cover posts sent through Fast Scheduler only.

help.channel_manage.content.en: Everything about one channel lives in two places: the Channels list and the channel's own info screen. Channels (main menu) lists every channel you have connected. For each channel you get: • The channel name. • Time Zone — posts for this channel are sent in the channel's own time zone, so you never juggle UTC offsets yourself. • Change Channel — replace this channel with a different one; its scheduled messages move with you. • Disconnect Channel — unlink the channel (see Remove a Channel). Tap a channel's → button for the details screen: connection role, sender bot, time zone, and how many scheduled and recurring messages the channel holds. Each channel is configured independently — ideal for multi-channel setups.

help.channel_permissions.content.en: For the bot to work, these admin permissions are needed: • Post Messages - required to send posts. • Edit Messages - recommended, for editing after posting. • Delete Messages - recommended, for cleanup. Add the bot as an administrator in channel settings and tick the permissions you want. Without Post Messages, scheduling will fail with a "bot is not admin" error.

help.channel_posting.content.en: Every post in your channel is delivered by a sender bot — that is what makes scheduling possible at all. This is not an optional nicety: the scheduler unlocks only after each connected channel has its own sender bot, because Telegram requires a bot to hold Post Messages rights in the channel it posts to. What this means in practice • Posts appear from your bot's name and avatar, not from @FastSchedulerBot — your brand stays in front of readers. • One bot per channel. A second channel needs a second bot (create as many as you like in @BotFather). • Free plan includes {bots_free} sender bot; Premium raises this to {bots_prem}. • If a send ever fails (say, the bot lost its admin rights), Fast Scheduler retries through the main bot so the post is not lost — and warns you to restore the bot's permissions. Connected a channel but not a bot yet? Open Bots → 🔑 I Have a Token and finish the pairing — scheduling, the calendar, and every other sending feature stay locked until then.

help.channel_remove.content.en: To unlink a channel: 1. Open Channels → find the channel. 2. Tap 🔗 Disconnect Channel → confirm. What happens to the channel's messages: • Scheduled messages on that channel are removed or reassigned to another connected channel — the bot tells you exactly how many. • Recurring messages are reassigned to another connected channel too; if none is connected, they stop. • If a sender bot was attached only to this channel, the bot notifies you that it no longer has a channel to post to. Re-connecting the channel later starts fresh — reconnect its sender bot before scheduling again. To delete individual messages, use Message List instead.

help.channel_signature.content.en: A signature is your custom footer (or header) — for example "Posted by @yourchannel" — added automatically when a post goes out. How: send /signature (or tap 📝 Signature on the review screen) → create a signature with ➕ Add Signature → choose its position (start or end of the post) and how many blank lines separate it from the content. When saving you can enable auto-add and pick the channels it should attach to. • Saved signatures are reusable — edit, re-position, or delete them from Saved Signatures. • Signatures are attached at send time, so your stored messages stay clean. • Free users can try the feature once; after that it is Premium. See also: Signature Position.

help.channel_stats.content.en: Premium users can view per-channel statistics and paginated leaderboards: top posts by views, comments, or reactions (up to 50 per page), plus a top-commentators ranking of the people who comment most on your posts. Filtering: combine metric (views / comments / reactions / commentators), period (today / week / month / year / all), and page size (10 / 25 / 50) — then flip pages with the pager buttons. Comment authors: to see who actually comments, add the bot to your channel's discussion group. Until then, the leaderboard shows a tip reminding you — once the bot is in the group, comments are attributed automatically. These stats help you learn what content performs best so you can schedule more of what works. Channel stats are available for every connected channel — shown in the main bot, or inside its sender bot.

help.connect_bot.content.en: Every channel needs its own sender bot - a Telegram bot you own that posts messages to your channel under the bot's name. Why Connect Your Own Bot? • Messages are sent from YOUR bot, not the main bot • Your bot's name and photo appear as the author • Professional appearance for your channel • Low sending delays — your messages go out through your bot, not the shared main bot queue • Detailed channel leaderboards — see most viewed, most reacted, and most commented posts for each channel How to Get a Bot Token 1. Open @BotFather on Telegram 2. Send /newbot and follow the instructions 3. Choose a name and username for your bot 4. Copy the token (format: 1234567890:ABCdef..._XYZ) 5. Never share your token with anyone you don't trust How to Connect 1. In Fast Scheduler, click Bots or use /bots 2. Click 🔑 I Have a Token 3. Send the bot token you copied from @BotFather 4. Select which channel this bot should send to 5. Make sure your bot is an Administrator in the target channel Limits • Free plan: 1 bot • Premium: up to 3 bots Managing Bots • Click Bots on the main menu to see all connected bots • You can replace a bot's token or disconnect it • Disconnecting a bot puts its channel back into "connect a sender bot" state — reconnect a bot to schedule again Inside Your Sender Bot • Management moves to the sender bot automatically when it is connected • Management → Hide Channel — strangers who start your bot won't see your channel name (Public Mode) • Management → Admins — give other people limited access to your channel • Statistics — open per-channel stats and leaderboards Troubleshooting • "Invalid token" — make sure you copied the FULL token from @BotFather • "Bot is not admin" — add your bot as an administrator in the channel • "Bot limit reached" — remove an existing bot or upgrade to Premium

Send the channel username: @yourchannel • Or forward any message from the channel • Or send an invite link • Or send the channel ID (e.g., -1001234567890) Multiple Channels • Free plan: 1 channel • Premium: up to 3 channels • Switch between channels at any time during scheduling Removing a Channel • Go to Connected Channel → click on the channel • Scheduled messages for that channel will be paused Common Errors • "Bot is not an admin" — add the bot as admin in channel settings • "Channel not found" — check the username/link is correct • "Invalid format" — use @username or full invite link

help.content_types.content.en: Here is everything you can send in your scheduled messages on the Free plan: ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Text ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ • Plain text or formatted text (bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, spoiler, code, links) • Inline buttons with <inline> syntax — add clickable links • Polls and quizzes (send a poll from any chat and forward it during scheduling — only anonymous polls work in channels) • Text-only messages (no media attached) ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Photos ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ • Single photos (JPEG, PNG) with optional caption • Photo albums (multiple photos grouped in one message — send them together during scheduling) • Random photo mode: send multiple photos, each message gets a random one • Sequential photo mode: photos assigned in order to your messages ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Videos ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ • Videos {max_video_free} each • Supported formats: MP4, MOV, AVI • Can be sent with or without a text caption ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ Documents & Files ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ • Any file type: PDF, DOC, XLS, ZIP, TXT, etc. • Animations (GIF) • Voice messages (OGG) • Audio files (MP3) ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ What Requires Premium ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ • Videos larger than {max_video_free} ({max_video_prem} on Premium) @@STORAGE@@• Media Storage videos (not allowed on Free) @@STORAGE@@• More than 1 Media Storage box (up to 20 on Premium) @@STORAGE@@• More than {storage_items_free} storage items ({storage_items_prem} on Premium) • Everything else works on the Free plan! Tip: To see your current plan limits, use /stats or check the Plan Limits help topic. @@STORAGE@@Need to send larger files? Upgrade to Premium with /premium to unlock {max_video_prem} video support and {storage_items_prem} storage.

help.edit.content.en: Change the content, schedule, or settings of an existing message. How to Access: • From Message List: preview a message, then tap Edit • Use /edit followed by a job ID What You Can Edit: Text — change the message content Date/Time — reschedule for a different time Media — add, change, or remove attached media Channel — send to a different channel Recurring Schedule — change daily/weekly/monthly settings Editing a Recurring Message: • You can change the time, day, or interval • Changes take effect immediately for all future sends • Past sends are not affected Duplicate a Message (⧾ /dub): • Use /dub to create an exact copy of a scheduled message • Useful for creating variations of the same post • The copy starts in edit mode so you can change the date/time See also: Message List and Delete Messages.

help.error_channel.content.en: • Bot is not an admin - add the bot as admin (Post Messages permission). • Channel not found - wrong username or link; verify @yourchannel. • Invalid format - use @username, a full invite link, or the numeric ID. • Can't connect - make sure you're the owner or an admin. Fix the cause and try connecting again.

help.error_common.content.en: • "Bot is not an admin" - add the bot as an administrator in the channel with Post Messages permission. • "Invalid token" - copy the FULL token from @BotFather, no extra spaces. • "Channel not found" - check the username/link; use @username or an invite link. • "Limit reached" - check /stats; delete old messages or upgrade. Most errors are fixed by one of these. See Troubleshooting for the full guide.

help.error_forbidden.content.en:
• "Bot was kicked from the chat" - re-add the bot as admin.
• "Bot can't post" - grant Post Messages permission.
• "Blocked by user" - the channel owner removed the bot; re-invite it.

These are Telegram permission errors - fix them in your channel settings, not in the bot.

help.getting_started.content.en: Three steps and your first post is scheduled. The whole setup usually takes five minutes. Step 1: Connect your channel Add @FastSchedulerBot as an administrator of your channel with at least the Post Messages permission. Then in the bot: Channels → Connect Channel, and send @yourchannel or simply forward any post from the channel. Step 2: Connect a sender bot — required Posts are delivered by your own bot; scheduling stays locked until every connected channel has one. Create a bot in @BotFather (/newbot), copy its token, and paste it in Bots → 🔑 I Have a Token. Then make your bot an administrator of the same channel, also with Post Messages. Step 3: Schedule your first message Tap 📅 Schedule a Message, enter the date and time (25.12.2025 10:00), type the post, preview, confirm. Done — it publishes itself. Each step has a detailed guide below, plus answers to the questions new users ask most.

help.glossary.content.en: Six terms cover most of the bot: • Channel — the Telegram channel your posts go to. The bot must be its admin. • Sender bot — your own bot that actually delivers the posts. Required for every channel; one bot per channel. • Scheduled message — a one-time post queued for a specific date and time. • Recurring message — a post that repeats (hourly, daily, weekly, monthly) until paused or deleted. • Signature — text appended to every post in a channel. • Premium — the paid plan: more channels and bots, unlimited sends, bigger media storage. Tap any term below for the full explanation.

help.glossary_channel.content.en: A Telegram channel is where your audience sees your posts. Fast Scheduler connects to your channel, then posts your scheduled and recurring messages to it. You must be the owner or an admin, and the bot must be an administrator with at least Post Messages permission. Free plan: {channels_free} channel. Premium: up to {channels_prem} channels, each with its own sender bot and time zone.

help.glossary_export.content.en: Export saves your data to a file you can download and keep. You can export scheduled and recurring messages, or run a full backup (.fsback) that restores everything - channels, bots, settings, media. Use Export from the main menu (or /export) for selective export, and /backup for a full backup.

Pay with Telegram Stars. See the Premium category for all details, including what happens when it expires.

help.glossary_recurring.content.en: A recurring message repeats automatically on a schedule - every day, on specific weekdays, or on a monthly date. Use it for regular content: daily tips, weekly digests, monthly reports, birthday wishes, reminders. Free plan: {recurring_free} recurring message. Premium: unlimited. To stop a recurring message, delete it from Message List.

help.glossary_sender.content.en: A sender bot is a Telegram bot you create via @BotFather. Fast Scheduler uses it to post messages so they appear from your bot's name. Every channel needs one sender bot - connecting it is required after the channel is connected. Benefits: your brand on every post, lower sending delay, per-channel statistics and leaderboards. Each sender bot is assigned to one channel. Free plan: {bots_free} bot. Premium: up to {bots_prem}.

help.glossary_signature.content.en: A signature is custom text that is automatically added to every message sent to your channel - for example "Posted by @yourbot" or your website link. It is a Premium feature. You can set the text, choose its position (start or end), and preview it before saving. When Premium expires, signatures are stripped from outgoing messages and removed at the final disconnect.

help.gs_step1.content.en: Open your channel settings → Administrators → Add Admin. Search for @FastSchedulerBot and add it. Give it at least Post Messages permission. For sender bots: also add your sender bot as admin. 2. Connect in Fast Scheduler Go back to the bot and click Channels → Connect Channel. You'll be asked to identify your channel. 3. Send channel info Send the channel username: @yourchannel Or forward a message from the channel. Or send an invite link: https://t.me/yourchannel Or send the channel numeric ID: -1001234567890 4. Done! The channel is now connected. Next, connect a sender bot (Step 2) — posting only works through your own bot. Troubleshooting "Bot is not an admin" — add the bot as admin in channel settings. "Channel not found" — double-check the username or link. "Invalid format" — use @username or a full invite link.

help.gs_step2.content.en: Every channel needs its own sender bot - it is required to post scheduled messages. Your own bot also makes posts appear from your bot's name. 1. Create a bot Open @BotFather in Telegram. Send /newbot and follow the prompts. Choose a name and username. Copy the token — it looks like: 1234567890:ABCdef..._XYZ 2. Enter the token In Fast Scheduler, click Bots → I Have a Token. Paste the token. The bot will be verified and connected automatically. 3. Assign to a channel Choose which channel this bot should send to. Make sure your bot is an Administrator in that channel (add it in channel settings with Post Messages permission). 4. Done! Messages will now be sent from your own bot. Limits Free: 1 bot. Premium: up to 3 bots. Common Issues "Invalid token" — copy the FULL token including the colon and all characters. "Bot is not admin" — add your bot as admin in the target channel. "Bot limit reached" — disconnect an existing bot or upgrade to Premium.

help.gs_step3.content.en: Click Schedule Message on the main menu or use the /schedule command. 2. Pick a channel If you have multiple channels, select one. If you have only one, this step is skipped. 3. Enter date/time Formats: DD.MM.YYYY HH:MM, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM Example: 25.12.2025 10:00 or 2025-12-25 10:00 You can also use 12-hour format: 25.12.2025 10:00 AM Or relative: tomorrow 09:00, today 18:00 Or just time: HH:MM or HH.MM — schedules for today (rolls to tomorrow if passed) 4. Send message content Type your message text. Use Telegram formatting: **bold**, __italic__, [text](url), etc. You can also send a photo with caption, video, document, poll, or voice message. 5. Add media (optional) Choose how to attach media: • Random — pick from multiple files (any mix: photos, videos, documents), each message gets a random one, sent with the right method for its type • Normal — one photo/video attached to every message • Sequential — files assigned in order @@STORAGE@@• From Storage — pick from saved media • None — text only 6. Confirm Review the details and confirm. Your message is now scheduled! Need multiple messages? Leave at least one empty line after each message: a date/time line, then your message, then a blank line, then the next dated message. You can repeat this as many times as you need — in one text or across several messages — and everything will be scheduled. A .txt upload with the same blank-line rule works too. Clickable buttons (optional) Add a button under your post with <inline>Button Text<link="https://example.com"> on its own line. Use -- between two buttons for side-by-side, // for a new row. Color a button with style="success" (green), style="primary" (blue) or style="danger" (red) inside the tag.

help.import_csv.content.en: CSV import turns a spreadsheet into scheduled messages — perfect for content plans prepared in Excel or Google Sheets. The format The file needs two columns: Date/Time and Content. Export your sheet as CSV (UTF-8) and send it to the bot during the import flow. Each row becomes one scheduled message; the date column accepts the same formats the bot accepts when typing (for example 25.12.2025 10:00). Where messages land Rows are imported into your connected channel — the import targets it directly, there is no channel picker. Times are interpreted in the channel's time zone. Tips for clean imports • Keep one message per row; put line breaks inside the Content cell. • Test with a two-row file first, review the result in the Message List, then import the full sheet. • Need richer structure (multiple channels, media)? Use .txt blocks or a full backup restore instead.

help.import_data.content.en: Import brings messages back into the scheduler from a file — the mirror image of Export. How to import 1. Open Data → Import (or send /import). 2. Send the file: a .fsback/.fspback backup, a .txt message list, a .csv spreadsheet, or a SetDate schedule. 3. For password-protected backups, enter the password when asked. 4. Confirm — full backups restore with an Overwrite or Add choice. Two kinds of import • Backup restore (from your own /backup files): everything comes back — scheduled and recurring messages, settings, channels, bots, media boxes. Overwrite replaces the current data; Add merges on top of it. • Message lists (.txt / .csv / SetDate): each block or row becomes a scheduled message in your connected channel, so make sure the channel is connected before you start. Before you confirm A full restore with Overwrite replaces your current data. If in doubt, run /export first (Premium) so you always have a way back.

help.import_formats.content.en: The import flow accepts: • .fsback / .fspback — full bot backups (restore with Overwrite or Add). • .txt — message lists; a blank line starts a new message, with the date on its own line (see the Format topic). • .csv — spreadsheets with Date/Time and Content columns. • SetDate files — schedules generated by @SetDate_bot, imported as-is. • .json — structured exports. Everything except full backups imports into your connected channel, in the channel's time zone. Connect the channel first, then import.

This keeps your content consistent without re-uploading files.

help.import_json.content.en: JSON import restores structured exports — including the exports made by this bot. Send the .json file during the import flow (Data → Import, or /import). The bot reads each record and recreates the scheduled message: text, date, and channel reference. If the file was exported from a different setup, messages land in your currently connected channel. Prefer a complete snapshot restore — settings, bots, recurring messages and all? A .fsback backup restore is the right tool; JSON is for message-level transfers.

help.language_add.content.en: The bot ships in several languages, and English is always available. If yours isn't in the list yet: Check the full list Open Language (or /language) and scroll — the menu shows every currently supported language, and new ones are added over time. Request a translation Ask via Feedback in the bot or write to @MaximalXP and tell us which language you need. Popular requests get prioritised. In the meantime • English commands like /schedule and /list work no matter which language is active. • Your channel content is never translated — only the bot's interface language changes. • @SetDate_bot shares your language preference, so both bots switch together once your language is added.

help.media_retention.content.en:
All media you send to the bot is automatically compressed — this shrinks the file Telegram stores and sends, and keeps it within your plan's size limits. Compression Comparison 
Feature            │ Free               │ Premium
───────────────────┼────────────────────┼───────────────────────
Photo max          │ {free_photo_max_dim}px            │ {premium_photo_max_dim}px
Photo quality      │ Q{free_photo_quality}               │ Q{premium_photo_quality}
Video max          │ {free_video_max_dim}p              │ {premium_video_max_dim}p
Video CRF          │ {free_video_crf}                 │ {premium_video_crf}
Video bitrate      │ {free_video_bitrate}bps             │ {premium_video_bitrate}bps
Audio bitrate      │ {free_audio_bitrate}                │ {premium_audio_bitrate}
Voice bitrate      │ {free_voice_bitrate}               │ {premium_voice_bitrate}
4K media           │ Blocked          │ Allowed
Compression is applied automatically when you upload media to: Media Storage, Scheduled / Recurring messages, Feedback attachments, Broadcasts, and anywhere else in the bot. Documents and stickers are stored as-is without compression. Media Retention & Cleanup The bot periodically removes old media references that are no longer needed: Ratings • Admin reply media in rating reviews: deleted after 30 days • The rating (stars, review text) stays forever Feedback / Support tickets • Attachments in closed / spam tickets: deleted after 30 days from closure • The conversation text stays forever Media Storage • Items are kept until you delete them manually • Never auto-deleted Scheduled Messages • Media reference is removed immediately after the message is sent • No data lingers Recurring Messages • Media stays until you delete the recurring message • Free accounts: recurring message expires after 1 year and is auto-removed

help.media_types.content.en: After sending your message text, you choose how media (photos, videos, etc.) is attached. 1. Random Mix Mode • Send multiple files during scheduling — photos, videos, documents, anything, even mixed together • Each scheduled message gets a random item from your collection, sent with the right method for its type • Different media each time — great for variety and engagement 2. Normal Photo Mode • Send one photo or video during scheduling • That single media is attached to every scheduled message • Simple and consistent — same image for all posts 3. Sequential Order • Send multiple media files in order • They are assigned in sequence to your messages • First media → first message, second → second, etc. • After the last media, repeats from the first • Choose order by date (upload time) or sent (input order) @@STORAGE@@4. From Storage @@STORAGE@@• Use media you've saved in Media Storage • Pick from your saved collection • Saves time if you reuse media across multiple schedules 5. No Media • Text-only messages • No photos, videos, or files attached Tips: • For photo albums, send multiple photos in one batch using Normal mode • Videos must be under plan limits (Free: {max_video_free}, Premium: {max_video_prem}) • You can mix text-only and media messages in the same batch

help.message_list.content.en: View, preview, edit, and delete all your scheduled and recurring messages. How to Access: • Click Message List on the main menu or use /list • Pick a channel (if you have multiple) What You See: • Scheduled messages — shown with date, time, and preview • Recurring messages — shown with schedule info (daily/weekly/monthly) • Media type — photo, video, document, or text-only What You Can Do: • Preview — see the full message content and settings • Edit — change text, media, date/time, or channel • Pause/Resume — temporarily stop a recurring message without deleting it • Delete — remove individual messages • Delete All — remove all messages at once • Delete by ID — remove a specific job ID Pagination: Messages are shown 10 per page. Use Previous / Next to browse. See also: Edit Messages, Delete Messages, and Pause & Resume.

help.ms_copy.content.en: Copy places a duplicate of an item into another box while the original stays where it is — unlike Move, which relocates the item. When copying beats moving • A logo that belongs to several campaign boxes at once. • Seasonal collections that share evergreen assets. • A "favourites" box that mirrors items from working boxes. Copies are independent: editing or deleting one copy never affects the other, and every schedule that references either box keeps working.

help.premium_expiry.content.en: When your Premium subscription ends, nothing is deleted on day one. You get a grace period, reminders, and a chance to choose what to keep. The timeline at a glance: • Before expiry: you receive reminders at 7, 3 and 1 day(s) left. • Day 0: a "Choose What to Keep" menu appears - pick up to {channels_free} channel, {bots_free} bot and {recurring_free} recurring message, plus (if you use it) the media storage box you want to keep. • Days 1-2: everything still works normally; you can change your choices. • Day 3: you get a final warning and an automatic backup file (.fsback). • Day 4: messages to the channels you did NOT keep stop sending. Your kept channel keeps working. • Day 17: media cleanup - non-kept storage boxes are deleted and the kept box is trimmed to {storage_items_free} items (videos first). • Day 35 + 12 h: final warning, then excess channels and sender bots are disconnected and their data removed. Signatures are deleted. Good news: renew at any point before the final disconnect and everything restores instantly - channels, bots, messages and media. See the sub-topics below for the grace period, frozen assets, renewal and refunds.

help.premium_freeze.content.en: When Premium expires, the assets that don't fit your free plan are frozen first and disconnected later - they are NOT deleted at once. What gets frozen: • Channels beyond the free limit stop receiving messages after day 3. • Sender bots of frozen channels are turned off. • Recurring messages beyond the free limit are paused. @@STORAGE@@• Media storages you didn't choose are deleted on day 17. • Signatures are stripped from outgoing messages and removed at disconnect. What keeps working: • Your kept channel and its sender bot continue as normal. • Scheduled messages on the kept channel keep sending. • Your account, settings, language and referral days remain. Reactivate Premium before the final disconnect to unfreeze everything instantly.

If you renew during the grace period, Premium is restored instantly and the expiry process is cancelled. After the grace period ends (day 3), the limits from your keep-selection start being applied.

help.premium_refund.content.en: Premium is paid in Telegram Stars, and Stars purchases are final under Telegram's own rules. Outside mandatory consumer rights, refunds are discretionary and granted case by case — typically for a double charge or a technical fault on our side. To request a refund, email fastschedulebot@gmail.com with: • The transaction ID (in the Stars payment confirmation or Settings → Payments). • Your Telegram username. • The purchase date and a short reason. We acknowledge requests within 7 business days. Approved refunds return through Telegram only; referral days and promo free periods have no monetary value and are never refundable. To stop future billing on a monthly plan, cancel via /premium — the paid period stays active until its end date.

Refunds are reviewed individually and are not guaranteed. If a payment is reversed by your bank/provider, Premium is revoked automatically and your account may be restricted until the issue is resolved.

help.premium_renew.content.en: Renewing restores your full Premium account - usually instantly. How to renew: 1. Open Premium (main menu or /premium). 2. Tap Pay Again or choose a plan. 3. Pay with Telegram Stars. 4. Premium activates immediately after payment confirms. If you're in the middle of the expiry process: • Before day 4: everything is restored, nothing is lost. • Between day 4 and day 35: excess channels/bots were frozen but still connected - they are restored. • After day 35: excess channels and bots were disconnected; you re-connect them manually after renewing. Auto-renew: monthly Stars plans renew automatically. Yearly Stars plans are one-time payments - you renew manually.

help.privacy.content.en: What the bot stores and why: • Telegram identifiers — your user ID and channel IDs, so the bot knows what it manages and for whom. • Content you schedule — message texts and media references, kept only to deliver your posts on time. • Settings — language, time zone, signatures, bot tokens you connect. • Operational logs — delivery results, used to fix failures and show you statistics. The bot never reads channels it is not connected to, never posts anything you did not schedule, and never shares your data with third parties. Deleting a message in the bot deletes it from storage; deleting your account deletes everything. Full details are in the website Privacy Policy.

help.recurring_uses.content.en: Recurring messages handle most repeat-posting needs. A few common ways to use them: Daily Digest Send a daily roundup every morning: 1. Use Recurring Message, set it to repeat every day. 2. Enter the send time, e.g. 09:00. 3. Write the digest content (or use the SetDate bot to prepare a full month). Event Reminder Remind your audience about an event: • Schedule an announcement at the event time. • Add reminder posts: -1 day, -3 hours, -10 minutes. • Use inline buttons for "Add to calendar" or "Buy ticket". News Roundup Post a daily or weekly news roundup: • Create a recurring message that runs on weekdays. • Use SetDate to preload a month of news scripts. • Attach a header image from your media storage. Promo Blast Schedule a promotion across channels: • Write the promo and add inline buttons ("Shop", "Learn more"). • Schedule it at your best posting time per channel. • Add follow-up reminders on days 2 and 5. Daily Quote Post a quote every morning: • Use a recurring daily message at 08:00. • Prepare a month of quotes in SetDate and import them. • Optionally attach a matching image from storage.

help.recurring_pause_resume.content.en: Pause and resume recurring messages without deleting them. How to Pause: 1. Open Message List (or use /list) 2. Select Recurring Messages 3. Find the message you want to pause 4. Tap the ⏸ button next to it 5. Confirm the pause What Happens When Paused: • The message stops sending immediately • The message is NOT deleted — it stays in your list • The schedule is preserved • You can see it marked as 'Paused' in the list How to Resume: 1. Open Message List 2. Select Recurring Messages 3. Find the paused message (marked with ⏸ Paused) 4. Tap the ▶ button next to it 5. Confirm the resume What Happens When Resumed: • The message starts sending again on its schedule • No content or settings are lost • The next send happens at the next scheduled time Use Cases: • Seasonal content — pause holiday posts when out of season • Temporary breaks — pause during vacations or events • Testing — pause to review content before going live • Rotation — pause one message while another takes priority Tip: Pausing is better than deleting if you might want to use the message again later.

help.referral_verify.content.en: To unlock the Referral Program you must connect a channel and schedule at least {referral_min_messages} message. This is not bureaucracy — it is how we verify your account is real. Why we do it. Every referral reward is paid out as Premium time, and Premium time costs us real money (Telegram Stars fees and server costs). Without verification, anyone could spin up dozens of empty accounts in minutes and drain the reward pool — which would force us to shut the program down for everyone, including honest users. What counts as verification. Connecting a channel proves you have something real to post to; scheduling a message proves you actually use the bot. Both checks are automatic and take most users under two minutes: send your channel link in Step 1 of the tutorial, then schedule any post — even a test message to yourself counts. What we check — and what we don't. We only look at anonymous counters (channels connected, messages created). We never read your message contents, never ask for documents or phone numbers, and never share anything with third parties. Verification is purely about activity, not identity. Common confusion. Opening the Referral menu before verifying shows a locked screen — that is expected, not a bug. Finish the two steps above and the menu unlocks by itself; nothing else is required.

help.referral_beta.content.en: The Referral Program is currently in BETA. It works end to end — links, tracking, crediting and day activation are all live — but you may occasionally run into rough edges: a counter that updates with a delay, a list that needs a reopen to refresh, or a message that reads slightly differently from what you expected. Your earned days are safe. Beta status affects polish, never balances. Every qualifying referral is recorded the moment it happens, and Premium days, once earned, are never lost because of a display glitch. If something looks wrong, reopen the /referral menu first — most counters refresh on open. Help us finish it. If you spot an error, tell us through /feedback with what you did step by step and, if possible, a screenshot. Beta reporters directly shape the final version: unclear texts get rewritten and confusing flows get simplified because of your reports. What may change. Reward sizes, limits and rules can still be tuned while the program is in beta. Any change will be announced in the referral menu itself — earned balances are always honored under the rules that were live when they were earned.

help.referral_credit.content.en: Here is exactly what happens from click to Premium days, for both sides. 1. Click. A new user opens your link and starts the bot. The click is recorded instantly, but nothing is granted yet — this is what the "pending" state in your list means. 2. Verify. The new user connects a channel and schedules at least {referral_min_messages} message — the same verification you completed to unlock the program. Until then, the referral stays pending. 3. Credit. The moment they qualify, both of you receive 3 Premium days: the days land in your referral balance (see them with /referral under Available days). If you already have paid Premium, the days wait in your balance until it ends. 4. Activate. On the free plan, activate earned days from the referral menu — a Premium period starts immediately. Used days move to the Used counter so you always see earned, used and available totals. Limits. Each user can generate referral rewards from up to 15 referees, i.e. a 45-day total. One referral per user — the same newcomer can never credit you twice, even if they click your link again.

help.schedule_one_time.content.en: A one-time scheduled message is sent exactly once at the date and time you choose. How to create one: 1. Tap Schedule Message (or /schedule) and pick the channel. 2. Send your message in blocks: a date-time line, the message text on the next line, then a blank line before the next block — three blocks means three messages. 3. Choose the Photo Mode (skip / attach normally / random from storage / sequential). 4. Check the Review screen and confirm. The bot replies with the queued job IDs and times — everything is editable or deletable from Message List until the moment of sending. Use it for announcements, promos and reminders; for repeating posts use Recurring Messages instead.

help.scheduling.content.en: Everything about one-time scheduling: the basic flow, every content type the bot can post, and the tools to manage what you have queued. The basic flow 1. Tap Schedule Message (or send /schedule). 2. Pick the channel — the bot you paired with it will do the posting. 3. Enter the date and time: use the format DD.MM.YYYY HH:MM (for example 25.12.2025 10:00) or send it in the same message as the text. 4. Send the message content — plain text or with photos, videos, documents, polls, stickers, voice, locations. 5. Review the preview and confirm. The post goes out automatically at the chosen time, in the channel's time zone. Before scheduling works at all, two things must be connected: the channel (bot as admin) and its sender bot — see Getting Started if you are not there yet. Managing the queue Everything you schedule lands in the Message List and Calendar: preview before it posts, edit any detail, or delete what changed. The topics below cover each content type and every management tool.

help.sender_bot_management.content.en: A sender bot is more than a posting tool — it is also a full management interface for your channel. How it works When you connect a sender bot to a channel, management moves to it automatically — no extra setup. The main bot then shows a restricted menu (or a private "Public Mode" view if you hide the channel), while the full dashboard lives inside your bot. Inside the sender bot (Management menu) • Hide / Show Channel — in Public Mode your channel name is hidden from strangers who start the bot; they only see a generic welcome and an Open Main Bot button. • Admins — grant other Telegram accounts limited access to your channel: scheduling, viewing stats, or managing settings (RBAC). • Channel admins open the same bot and see exactly the tools their role allows — nothing more. Restore to the main bot? Not needed. Management stays with the sender bot; if the bot's token ever breaks, Fast Scheduler falls back to the main bot for delivery so posts are never lost.

help.setdate.content.en: Need to schedule many posts at once? The SetDate Bot lets you bulk-create schedules in minutes. What is SetDate? SetDate is a companion bot that helps you create multiple scheduled messages quickly. Instead of entering each message one by one, you prepare all messages in SetDate and import them in one click. How It Works 1. Click Open SetDate during the scheduling flow 2. The SetDate bot opens with your context 3. Set a start date and how many posts per day 4. Define posting times (e.g., 09:00, 14:00, 18:00) 5. Send your text messages — one per block separated by blank lines (or one by one, then Done); .txt upload works too, media is added later during import 6. Generate a schedule file 7. Click Import to Fast Scheduler 8. You return to Fast Scheduler with all messages pre-loaded 9. Choose media options and confirm Benefits • Schedule 10, 50, or 100+ posts in just a few minutes • Auto-assigns dates and times to each message • Supports European and American date formats • Supports inline buttons with custom layouts • Plain-text posts; button markup carries over to Fast Scheduler Features • Flexible time parsing: 08:00, 2:00 PM, 12;00 • Upload .txt files with your posts • Download your schedule as .txt, .csv, or .json • Summary with dates and totals plus downloads before importing • One-click import back to Fast Scheduler Language Sync Both bots share your language preference. When you change the language in one, the other bot sends you a message asking if you want to sync the change — tap Yes to apply it.

help.signature.content.en: Add a custom signature — for example "Posted by @yourbot" — to every post on the channels you choose. How to set up: 1. Tap 📝 Signature on the main menu or send /signature. 2. Use Add Signature and send your signature text (bold, italic, code and links work). 3. Pick the position — start or end of the post — and how many blank lines separate it. 4. Enable auto-add and select the channels it should attach to; or add it per message from the signature list. Good to know: • Signatures are appended at send time — your stored messages stay clean. • They never take over your inline button rows. • Free users can try signatures once; after that it is a Premium feature. When Premium expires: auto-add stops once Premium is gone, and signature settings are deleted when the expiry process fully completes. Reactivate Premium to keep everything.

help.schedule_advanced.content.en: Beyond the basic flow, the scheduler covers a set of practical extras. Here is the complete picture. Editing scheduled messages Everything about a pending message stays editable until the moment it is sent: open the Message List, tap the message, and choose 🔄 Replace (or use /edit with the job ID). You can change the text, the date and time, the attached media, and even the target channel. The bot shows a fresh preview before saving. Deleting messages Pending messages can be removed one by one from the Message List, via /delete, or by job ID. Delete All wipes every scheduled and recurring message for a channel at once — use it with care, the bot asks for confirmation first. Scheduling forwardable content Anything you can forward inside Telegram can be scheduled: forward a post from another channel while scheduling, and the bot copies its text and media into your own post. Polls and quizzes work the same way: create the poll in any chat and forward it to the bot during scheduling (or create it inline in the bot if your Telegram version supports poll sending), then pick a date. Only anonymous polls may post in channels — that is a Telegram rule for channels, not a bot limit. Special content types • Location and venues — send the location during scheduling. • Voice messages and video notes — recorded or forwarded as usual. • Animated GIFs and stickers — stickers can even carry a text caption, posted right after the sticker. Time zones Every date you enter is interpreted in the channel's time zone, so a channel with an international audience posts exactly when its readers are awake. Set or check it under Channels → the channel → Time Zone, or with /timezone.

schedule.prompt.en:
📝 Schedule a Message Send me your message with the date and time. Format: DD.MM.YYYY HH:MM Your message Examples: 25.12.2026 15:30 Happy Holidays! 25.12.2026 20:00 Evening post Features: • Add photos, videos, or documents • Create polls and quizzes (anonymous only) • Add inline buttons • Use formatting (bold, italic, links, etc.) 📌 Inline Buttons: Add clickable buttons to your message: <inline>Button Text<link="https://example.com"> Use -- to place buttons side by side, and // to start a new row. Button colors: add style="success" (green), style="primary" (blue) or style="danger" (red) inside the button tag.
📝 Notes • Premium emojis are not supported. • Documents are supported. • Telegram Date formatting and Articles are not yet supported. • Checklists are not supported. • Any Premium-only feature is not yet supported. • Multiple messages at once: separate each message with an empty line — a date/time line, then your message, then a blank line, then the next one. You can send as many scheduling messages as you need, one after another — every batch adds to your queue. • Supported: text, photos, videos, animations, voice, audio (music), location/venue, documents, polls (anonymous only), stickers.

help.ms_bulk.content.en: Reorganizing a box item by item is slow. Premium adds three bulk tools inside any open box: Move All • Moves every item (or only one type: images, videos, files) into a box you pick. • Use it to split a mixed box by type or to retire a finished campaign in one tap. Copy All • Same flow, but the source box keeps its items — handy for seeding a new campaign box from an archive without touching the original. Download Box • Saves the whole box as a single archive, so you can keep an offline copy or hand assets to a teammate. On Free, open any item and use Move, Copy, or Download for one file at a time.

help.legal_update.content.en: In October 2026 the three legal documents were rewritten for clarity — no new data collection, no new fees, no change to what the bot does: • Privacy Policy — now names every service explicitly (Fast Scheduler, SetDate, Support bot, website) and lists exactly what is stored and why. Your rights are unchanged: export a copy anytime (/export, full backup with /backup on Premium) and delete everything on request. • Terms of Service — clearer plan and fair-use rules, plus how material changes are announced (in-app notice; continued use after the effective date means acceptance). • Refund Policy — spelled out for Telegram Stars: Stars purchases are final under Telegram's own rules, with discretionary refunds for genuine failures (double charge, technical fault). Request via fastschedulebot@gmail.com; we acknowledge within 7 business days. Each document shows its effective date, and previous versions stay available in the version history on the website.
